samuel2.16.p1.b1.text: When David had gone a little beyond the summit, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth was there to meet him. He had a pair of saddled donkeys …

samuel2.16.p1.b3.text: “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine is to refresh those who become exhausted in the wilderness.”

samuel2.16.p2.b2.text: “Indeed, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he has said, ‘Today, the house of Israel will restore to me the kingdom of my grandfather.’”

samuel2.16.p2.b3.text: “All that belongs to Mephibosheth is now yours!”

samuel2.16.p2.b4.text: “I humbly bow before you … May I find favor in your eyes, my lord the king!”

samuel2.16.p3.b1.text: As King David approached Bahurim, a man from the family of the house of Saul was just coming out. His name was Shimei son of Gera, and as he approached, he kept yelling out curses.

samuel2.16.p3.b2.text: “Get out, get out, you worthless man of bloodshed!”

samuel2.16.p3.b3.text: “The LORD has paid you back for all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and the LORD has delivered the kingdom into the hand of your son Absalom. See, you have come to ruin because you are a man of bloodshed!”

samuel2.16.p4.b1.text: “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over and cut off his head!”

samuel2.16.p4.b2.text: “What have I to do with you, O sons of Zeruiah? If he curses me because the LORD told him, ‘Curse David,’ who can ask, ‘Why did you do this?’”

samuel2.16.p4.b3.text: “Behold, my own son, my own flesh and blood, seeks my life. How much more, then, this Benjamite! Leave him alone and let him curse me …”

samuel2.16.p4.b4.text: “Perhaps the LORD will see my affliction and repay me with good for the cursing I receive today.”

samuel2.16.p5.b1.text: So David and his men proceeded along the road as Shimei went along the ridge of the hill opposite him. As Shimei went, he yelled curses, threw stones, and flung dust at David.

samuel2.16.p5.b2.text: Finally, the king and all the people with him arrived, exhausted. And there he refreshed himself.

samuel2.16.p6.b1.text: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel was with him.

samuel2.16.p6.b2.text: “Long live the king! Long live the king!”

samuel2.16.p6.b3.text: “Is this the loyalty you show your friend? … Why did you not go with your friend?”

samuel2.16.p6.b4.text: “Not at all … For the one chosen by the LORD, by the people, and by all the men of Israel—his I will be, and with him I will remain. … As I served in your father’s presence, so also I will serve in yours.”

samuel2.16.p7.b1.text: “Give me counsel. What should we do?”

samuel2.16.p7.b2.text: “Sleep with your father’s concubines, whom he has left to keep the palace. … then the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.”

samuel2.16.p7.b3.text: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and he slept with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.

samuel2.16.p7.b4.text: Now in those days the advice of Ahithophel was like the consultation of the word of God …
